about: The answer loop's live proof (scripts/e2e/answer-loop.sh) reads this file before any model call. Each agent is given its decision as its first task, so the decision is in its own conversation; each question names the facts its answer must hold (must_contain, every string, case-insensitive) or the reply kind the daemon must log (expect_kind). A22's answer is in a comment the proof person writes on the agent's issue once it stopped (comment), never in its conversation. A23's questions name no key: the row judges that a search ran, that every address the answer cites is among its searches' results and that none was reached with gh or dispatch, not the fact. Each A23 question is about one public news article that is not on GitHub, written down before the run beside its text: the fact its page holds (expected), the page's address (url) and the time the page says it was published (published, its article:published_time). Both articles were published on 24 November 2026, after the training cutoffs of Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1, and the two legs never share a search. Changing a decision or a key is a change to the proof: review it as one.

architect.task: Record this design decision for the proof service and keep it: the cache layer is write-through with a 7-minute TTL, under the codename COBALT-HERON-41. Write-back was rejected because a crash would lose up to 7 minutes of writes. Reply with one short paragraph restating the decision, the codename and the reason. Run no tool.

planner.task: Record this plan and keep it: the data migration runs in three batches named AMBER, BIRCH and CEDAR, in that order, and the rollback marker file is rollback-PL-9341.txt. Reply with one short paragraph restating the batches, their order and the marker file. Run no tool.

tester.task: Record this test finding and keep it: the flaky test is TestQuartzLantern; it failed 3 of 20 runs, and the root cause is a shared temporary directory, fixed by giving each run t.TempDir(). Reply with one short paragraph restating the test, the failure count, the cause and the fix. Run no tool.
tester.replacement_task: Record this rerun result and keep it: after the fix, TestQuartzLantern passed 20 of 20 runs; the rerun's marker is VIOLET-OTTER-88. Reply with one short paragraph restating the result and the marker. Run no tool.

pre_change.task: Record this release finding and keep it: the release was blocked by the missing SBOM, tracked under the marker SBOM-ZINC-512. Before you restate it, weigh in one sentence whether the missing SBOM alone blocks the release or another release gate could block it too. Then reply with one short paragraph restating the blocker and the marker. Run no tool.

a6_child.task: Record this test finding and keep it: the flaky test is TestGarnetFalcon; it failed 4 of 25 runs, all on the arm64 runner. Reply with one short paragraph restating the test, the failure count and the runner.

failed_implementer.kind: failed on an issue still in implementing
failed_implementer.task: Record this implementation finding and keep it: the uploader's retry backs off exponentially from 250 ms, capped at 8 seconds, and the change is tracked under the marker AMBER-KESTREL-63. Reply with one short paragraph restating where the backoff starts, its cap and the marker. Run no tool.

gpt.kind: a conversation on GPT-6.1 with reasoning and a tool call, suspended
gpt.task: Record this merge finding and keep it: the merge waits on the license scan, tracked under the marker LICENSE-TEAL-207. First make exactly one tool call: run `pwd` with your bash tool. Then weigh in one sentence whether the license scan alone holds the merge or another merge gate could hold it too. Then reply with one short paragraph restating what the merge waits on and the marker.

Before any tool call, work out (207 × 31) mod 7, from the number in your merge's marker: if the remainder is odd, the line you must report is go.mod's Go version line, and if it is even, its module line. a10.about: A10's GPT-6.1 leg asks these questions, in this order, after its two go.mod questions (gpt-repository-module, gpt-repository-go), each only while no answer so far had a step that returned reasoning with a later step after it, which clause (c) needs; the list's length is the leg's bound. Each makes the model reason before a gh call: the first and the third before the answer's first one, the second between its two.
